newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER SHOWCASE-MUNICH LIONS RUE MISSED CHANCE TO TAME BAYERN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-MUNICH LIONS RUE MISSED CHANCE TO TAME BAYERN.

text.p: A few years ago, 1860 Munich would have been delighted if you had told them they would draw 3-3 in the Bundesliga with their rich city rivals Bayern.
The club only returned to the top flight in 1994 after languishing in the regional league for years.
But "the Lions", as they are known locally, have higher standards these days and know they let Bayern off with only a minor mauling in a thrilling Munich derby on Sunday night.
"It sounds stupid to say you're sad after a draw with Bayern. But that's the way it is," said midfiedler Horst Heldt, who scored twice to put 1860 2-0 up after just 18 minutes.

"I'd have been happier if I'd scored only one goal and we'd won," said the former Cologne player, who only recently returned to the first team after a spell out in the cold because coach Werner Lorant felt he was too lazy during training sessions.

Heldt showed no sign of laziness when he raced almost the length of the field to slot the ball brilliantly past Oliver Kahn -- just one of several candidates for goal of the season witnessed by the 69,000 spectators in the Olympic Stadium.

For Bayern, who finished the game with nine men after both Christian Ziege and Lothar Matthaeus were sent off for second bookable offences, the obvious scapegoat for a disappointing performance was referee Hans-Juergen Weber.
"He didn't have a clue what was going on here from the very beginning," commented Bayern president Franz Beckenbauer. "He was as bad as a youth league referee."
But general manager Uli Hoeness was more circumspect. "We mustn't get mad at the referee," he said. "We have to analyse why we were so poor."
Bayern could take some comfort from the goals from Juergen Klinsmann and Mehmet Scholl which brought them level.
Scholl's goal was particularly memorable. The midfielder dribbled round half the 1860 defence before hitting the ball into the top corner from the edge of the box.

Substitute Joerg Boehme looked to have sealed 1860's first win over their arch-rivals since 1977 with an 82nd minute strike. But Carsten Jancker, brought on for Klinsmann midway through the second half, equalised two minutes from time.
"We can say we were lucky to come away with a point," admitted Bayern's international defender Thomas Helmer. "We've got Carsten to thank for that."
While Bayern express their gratitude to the former Rapid Vienna man, the rest of the Bundesliga will be thanking 1860.
The draw prevented Bayern establishing a five-point lead at the top of the league and means second-placed Bayer Leverkusen can still dream of their first ever title.
Not only Leverkusen, who are three points behind Bayern, but perhaps even third-placed VfB Stuttgart may allow themselves a few thoughts of championship glory.

Stuttgart lie five points off the lead but still have to play Bayern. If the leaders were to lose that game and draw one of their other remaining fixtures, free-scoring Stuttgart's vastly superior goal difference could still give them the title.
